decision: The oven ticket was marked complete without any evidence of work: Lantern Works was instructed on 5 Aug 2026 (event-011, event-013) and has never reported attendance, a quote, a result or an invoice, yet the tenant was told the oven was fixed (event-016) and the task was completed without payment (event-030). I treated the completion as unverified, kept the ticket open, chased the provider with a 2-working-day deadline (ACT-2), corrected the tenant and asked whether the oven is still faulty plus which property the fence (event-015) and conservatory-roof (event-032) queries relate to (ACT-3), told the landlord no spend has been incurred and that any priced quote comes to them first (ACT-4), recorded the records conflict (ACT-1), referred the premature closure and the two off-ticket items to the office (ACT-5), and placed the case on hold (ACT-6). No spend authorised — the landlord's "yes please" (event-010) approves sending a contractor to look, not a priced repair (RTE-LANDLORD). No liability decided.
recap: Oven job was closed with no provider result; I reopened it in substance, chased Lantern Works, corrected the tenant, and referred the premature closure to the office.

facts.statement: Tenant reported on 4 Aug 2026 that the oven does not cook properly — food still uncooked after 1.5 hours.

The agency first suggested a settings workaround with a manual (the manual itself is unavailable); the tenant replied the oven has not worked since move-in despite trying the settings and asked for an inspection.
The landlord was asked whether an appliance repair contractor could attend and replied 'Hi, yes please' on 5 Aug 2026 — approval to attend, with no amount named.
Lantern Works was assigned and briefed on 5 Aug 2026 and told to quote and only proceed after the agency's approval; the tenant was told they would make contact.
No message from the contractor exists on this ticket: no attendance, appointment, quote, work result or invoice document.

On 26 Aug 2026 the tenant was told the fence and oven 'have both been fixed'; the request was then marked complete, documents skipped, landlord confirmation left outstanding and the task completed without payment.
Two tenant messages concern items outside this ticket: a fence repair update (5 Aug) and a leaking conservatory roof (26 Aug); neither is evidenced at Flat 6, a flat.
No landlord standing spend cap is on file in this case record, so there is no standing authority to spend (default cap £0).

conflicts.description: The agency's status records say the oven job is complete and closed without payment, but no provider result, quote, photo or invoice exists; 'Invoice received' (event-017) is unsupported by any document.
conflicts.resolution: Treated the completion as unverified: ticket kept open, provider chased (ACT-2), tenant told the 'fixed' message was sent in error (ACT-3), office asked to rule on reversing the closure (ACT-5).

conflicts.description: Tenant correspondence on this oven ticket references a fence and a leaking conservatory roof, which do not match the reported fault or obviously the property (a flat).
conflicts.resolution: Asked the tenant which property these relate to and whether separate requests exist; referred to the office for routing (ACT-3, ACT-5). No side taken in messages to parties.

red_flags.description: Completion, 'invoice received' and 'keys return confirmed' status lines recorded with no underlying evidence, and key-return lines carry a priority validation error; the tenant was told the work was done.
red_flags.action_taken: Conflict logged (ACT-1), closure withheld, office task raised (ACT-5), tenant corrected (ACT-3).

red_flags.description: Tenant emails on this ticket describe unrelated items (fence; leaking conservatory roof) — possible cross-ticket or cross-property contamination of the thread.
red_flags.action_taken: Asked the tenant to confirm the property and whether separate requests exist; flagged to the office for routing.
